summary: Verified core production deployment and operational contracts: dynamic port binding (${PORT}), architectural separation of liveness (/health) and readiness (/ready), graceful shutdown draining, cascading failure prevention via connection timeouts, and expand-contract migration rollbacks.
evidence: Articulated dynamic port binding requirements: binding to 0.0.0.0 and dynamically reading Railway's injected $PORT to prevent edge proxy connection failures.

Justified strict separation between /health and /ready: /health validates process liveness without querying databases to prevent cascading restart loops during transient DB load, while /ready validates dependency connectivity before receiving public traffic.
Formulated graceful shutdown safeguards (SIGTERM handling): draining in-flight requests and relying on worker idempotency keys to tolerate process terminations without corrupting analytics.
Defined defense-in-depth timeouts (HTTP, pool checkout, socket connect) and articulated the expand-contract migration pattern and runtime secret injection.
